mainEntity.name: Should I choose an attached in-law addition or a detached guest suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in placement and physical connection to your main house. An attached in-law suite shares at least one wall with your primary residence, making it easy to share central utilities and provide quick indoor access to assist an aging family member. However, attached additions require careful architectural design to blend seamlessly with your home's existing roofline and exterior stucco or siding. A detached suite operates as a standalone building on your parcel, offering maximum privacy and noise separation for both households. The tradeoff is that detached builds demand independent utility trenching, distinct HVAC systems, and sufficient yard clearance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached suites offer shared utilities and quick indoor access, while detached suites provide total privacy but require independent utility trenching and more yard space.
